title: Affine etale solution sheaves under a local ringed-topos morphism
statement:
Work in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $A,B$ be commutative rings, $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], with small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] and structure sheaves $\mathcal O_X(T)=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ and $\mathcal O_Y(T)=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$. Let $g:(\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{et}}),\mathcal O_X)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(Y_{\mathrm{et}}),\mathcal O_Y)$ be a ringed-topos morphism [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Assume its square on the unit subsheaves $g^{-1}(\mathcal O_Y^\times)\to\mathcal O_X^\times$ and $g^{-1}\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal O_X$ is cartesian; the unit subsheaf consists of locally invertible sections. Let $\varphi:B\to A$ be the map on global sections induced by $g^\sharp$ (using $g^{-1}1=1$), and put $f=\operatorname{Spec}\varphi:X\to Y$. For an affine etale $Y$-scheme $V=\operatorname{Spec}C$, write $h_V(T)=\operatorname{Hom}_Y(T,V)$ [lem-weil-pbc-small-etale-representable-presheaf-sheaf]. There are isomorphisms of sheaves
$$\alpha_V:g^{-1}h_V\xrightarrow{\sim}h_{X\times_YV},$$
natural for every $Y$-morphism between affine etale $Y$-schemes. The fibre product is [def-pc-fibre-product]. For every $c\in C$, let $\operatorname{ev}_c:h_V\to\mathcal O_Y$ send $u:T\to V$ to $u^*c$, and let $\operatorname{ev}'_c:h_{X\times_YV}\to\mathcal O_X$ send $u:T\to X\times_YV$ to $(\operatorname{pr}_Vu)^*c$. Then
$$\operatorname{ev}'_c\alpha_V=g^\sharp\circ g^{-1}(\operatorname{ev}_c).$$
No isomorphism of inverse-image functors on all sheaves is assumed or asserted.

source.place: Tag 04I6 (lemma-morphism-ringed-etale-topoi-affines), proof from the construction of the global ring map through the polynomial equalizer, strictly henselian stalk comparison and functoriality diagrams, and final coordinate-compatibility diagram; the affine generator comparison only.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine] to $V\to Y$: $B\to C$ is an etale ring map, in particular finitely presented. By [lem-exc-etale-jacobian-presentation] choose a square presentation $C=B[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(P_1,\ldots,P_n)$ with Jacobian determinant a unit in $C$, in the precise sense of [def-exc-jacobian-presentation]. This is a global presentation of the given algebra, not a cover of $V$.

source.place: Tag 04I6, first paragraph after the global ring map; algebra.tex Tag 00U9 (lemma-etale-standard-smooth)

proof.text: For any $Y$-scheme $T$, [lem-a1-locally-ringed-space-affine-adjunction] identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_Y(T,V)$ with $B$-algebra maps $C\to\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$: the condition of being over $Y$ is equality of the maps on $B$, by naturality and injectivity of that same adjunction. The polynomial universal property [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and the quotient relations identify these maps with tuples satisfying $P_i=0$. Thus $h_V$ is the equalizer of polynomial evaluation and zero on $\mathcal O_Y^n$. By the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product], the same argument on $X$ identifies $h_{X\times_YV}$ with the solution equalizer for $P_i^\varphi$ on $\mathcal O_X^n$. These are sheaves by [lem-weil-pbc-small-etale-representable-presheaf-sheaf]. Inverse image preserves finite limits, and $g^\sharp$ preserves ring operations [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. For each polynomial, expand its finite sum of coefficient-monomial terms: applying $g^\sharp$ gives precisely evaluation of its coefficient image under $\varphi$, since $g^\sharp$ sends the pulled-back global section $b$ to $\varphi(b)$. Therefore the coordinate map $(g^\sharp)^n$ carries the pulled-back first equalizer to the second, giving a unique map $\alpha_V$ commuting with the coordinate inclusions.

source.place: Tag 04I6, polynomial equalizer and dotted-arrow construction

proof.text: Fix a geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$, with associated topos point $p$ [lem-fix-geometric-stalk-topos-point]. Put $q=g\circ p$. By [lem-trf-etale-topos-points-geometric] choose a geometric point $\bar y$ representing $q$, in an enlarged common universe if necessary. The composition comparison [lem-sfb-ringed-topos-pullback-stalk] identifies $(g^{-1}\mathcal O_Y)_p$ with $(\mathcal O_Y)_q$. Put $R=(\mathcal O_Y)_q$ and $S=(\mathcal O_X)_p$. Both are strict henselizations of ordinary local rings by the ring-isomorphism clause of [lem-sfb-etale-zariski-module-geometric-stalk], and hence strictly henselian by clause 3 of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples], applied at the maximal ideal of each local ring. The stalk of $g^\sharp$ is a ring map $\theta:R\to S$.

source.place: Tag 04I6, stalk comparison paragraph; Tag 04HU; Tag 04HX; algebra.tex Tags 04GW and 04GP

proof.text: The point inverse image preserves finite limits [lem-fix-geometric-stalk-topos-point]. For a commutative ring sheaf $H$, its unit subsheaf is isomorphic, by first projection, to the finite-limit object $\{(a,b)\in H^2:ab=1\}$: an inverse is unique and locally existing inverses glue. Applying $p^{-1}$ therefore identifies the stalk of the unit subsheaf with the units of the stalk ring; the same holds after applying $g^{-1}$. Apply $p^{-1}$ to the assumed cartesian unit square. It says exactly $\theta^{-1}(S^\times)=R^\times$. Thus $\theta$ is a local homomorphism as required by the solution-invariance lemma.

source.place: Tag 04I6, sentence asserting that the stalk map is local; finite-limit unpacking of the locality hypothesis

proof.text: The polynomial system over $R$ is obtained from $P_i$ via the global-section germ map $B\to R$. Its quotient has a square Jacobian presentation: if $D\Delta-1=\sum H_iP_i$ in $B[x]$ expresses an inverse of the determinant modulo the relations, applying $B\to R$ gives the same identity over $R$. Thus the determinant is a unit in the quotient over $R$, and [lem-exc-etale-jacobian-presentation] and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine] show its affine spectrum is etale over $\operatorname{Spec}R$. The coefficients in $S$ agree whether mapped through $B\to R\xrightarrow{\theta}S$ or $B\xrightarrow{\varphi}A\to S$, by the global-section compatibility in step 2. Since the point inverse image preserves the finite equalizers and products [lem-fix-geometric-stalk-topos-point], the stalk of $\alpha_V$ is precisely the coordinatewise $\theta$ map on these solution sets. Apply [lem-sfb-strict-henselian-etale-solutions] using steps 3 and 4 to obtain a bijection. This holds at every geometric point of $X$, so [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-iso-on-geometric-stalks] makes $\alpha_V$ an isomorphism. For empty $X$ the same conservative statement is vacuous and still gives the isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 04I6, isomorphism on stalks; algebra.tex Tag 04GX (lemma-strictly-henselian-solutions); Tag 03PU

proof.text: For a $Y$-map $V_1\to V_2$, write its algebra map $C_2\to C_1$ on the chosen generators as $x_{2,j}\mapsto Q_j(x_{1,1},\ldots,x_{1,n_1})$, with $Q_j\in B[x_{1,1},\ldots,x_{1,n_1}]$. Such lifts exist because the presentation of $C_1$ is a quotient of that polynomial ring. On solution equalizers the map of representables is exactly substitution by the $Q_j$. The ring-operation preservation of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism] gives $g^\sharp Q_j(z)=Q_j^\varphi(g^\sharp z)$, by the finite-sum expansion already written in step 2. Hence the two composites in the naturality square have equal coordinates in $\mathcal O_X^{n_2}$. The solution equalizer inclusion is injective, so the composites are equal. Taking the identity of $V$ with any two presentations in this argument also proves presentation independence. The substitutions and their coefficient maps are those of the polynomial universal property [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]; the geometric interpretation is the affine-target adjunction [lem-a1-locally-ringed-space-affine-adjunction].

source.place: Tag 04I6, functoriality diagrams, with the polynomial substitution argument made explicit

proof.text:
For $c\in C$ choose a polynomial representative $Q\in B[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$. In the solution descriptions, $\operatorname{ev}_c=Q(\operatorname{ev}_{x_1},\ldots,\operatorname{ev}_{x_n})$, and $\operatorname{ev}'_c$ is the corresponding $Q^\varphi$ evaluation. The defining coordinate square for $\alpha_V$ and preservation of $0,1,+,\cdot$ by $g^\sharp$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism] imply
$$\operatorname{ev}'_c\alpha_V=Q^\varphi\bigl(g^\sharp g^{-1}\operatorname{ev}_{x_1},\ldots,g^\sharp g^{-1}\operatorname{ev}_{x_n}\bigr)=g^\sharp g^{-1}(\operatorname{ev}_c).$$
Changing $Q$ by a sum of multiples of the $P_i$ changes neither side, since both tuples satisfy the relations. This proves the asserted equality for every $c$, including constants from $B$.

The delivery is a first split, with no repair note. Live and side-live still have the item unsplit, and the new id is not in either. The statement is kept verbatim. Its cartesian units-square hypothesis is the 'local morphism' of the parent lem-sfb-scheme-ringed-etale-reconstruction, whose step 4 uses exactly the natural isomorphisms and the evaluation identity. Step 1: global square Jacobian presentation from etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine and exc-etale-jacobian-presentation. Step 2: h_V as the equalizer on O_Y^n, using the LRS affine adjunction for every T in the etale site, the polynomial universal property and the fibre-product universal property (this avoids the unstated A⊗C presentation). The square commutes because g^♯ preserves ring operations and g^♯(g^{-1}b)=φ(b). Step 3: the geometric-stalk point; q=g∘p is a geometric point by trf-etale-topos-points-geometric; the pullback-stalk comparison identifies the rings; the ring-iso clause of etale-zariski-module-geometric-stalk with strict-henselization-triples clause 3 gives strict henselianity (the pairs and triples index categories are equivalent, a one-line step). Step 4, correctly marked elementary: units are the finite limit ab=1, so the stalk of the cartesian square gives θ^{-1}(S^×)=R^×. Step 5: the Jacobian identity base-changes to R, the coefficients agree, 04GX gives the stalk bijection, and the sets-on-geometric-stalks criterion finishes (empty X is vacuous). Steps 6 and 7: substitution naturality and the evaluation identity for every c, both elementary and correct. The new node lem-sfb-strict-henselian-etale-solutions is exactly 04GX, statement only and self-contained. I tested it at n=0, D=0, θ=id, x(x−1), x^2−u with 2u a unit, and Artin–Schreier.
